whatWasTriedFirst: MASTER_LIBRARY_SOURCE_DIR was exported at the pinned Master Library path.
The gitignored private/ tree was symlinked from the shared checkout, because some builders resolve the library as repoRoot/private and ignore that variable. That tree holds only the Master Library.
The committed corpus index was searched for the same bytes under any other custody: each of these SHA-256 values is indexed at exactly one path, and that path is in the unmounted recovery pool.
whatIsMissing.whatWouldUnblockIt: A container that mounts private/source-imports/Nationwide_Recovery_Pool_2026-09-02. The defects themselves are engineering defects in the shared Alabama and Illinois build hosts and need no legal or source research; they need the source bytes in order to be rebuilt, rehashed and re-measured.
whatIsMissing.whyNoCodeWasLandedAnyway: The mapping fixes are writable without the bytes, but they cannot be built, rehashed or measured here. Landing an unbuilt code change into hosts that other, unblocked containers rebuild would put this family's committed artifacts out of step with its builder and would move families this lane does not hold. That is the failure mode that left the Ohio companion undelivered in the first place.

fixBDispatch.dispatch: FIX-B repair cohort, lanes FIX06 / FIX07 / FIX08
fixBDispatch.familiesHeldByTheClaimLedger: The claim ledger, not the brief text, decided the scope. It grants FIX06 six families, FIX07 four and FIX08 three: thirteen, all FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED. The briefs name nine, seven and six. The ledger is authoritative per this dispatch, so the families named in a brief but not granted by the ledger were neither claimed nor read.
fixBDispatch.neverWriteVersusOwnedPathsContradiction: None found. Each brief's never-write list names nj-ordinance-set, ny-160-59-petition-set, pa-490-nonconviction-set and nj-indictable-conviction-set overlay paths, and none of those appears in any of the three owned-paths lists. Nothing was withheld on that ground.

ownedPathsDidNotCoverTheAssignedRepairs.finding: A different and real defect in the briefs: for several assigned families the owned-paths list names only a three-line shim, while the code carrying the measured defect lives in a shared build host the list does not name at all.
examples: FIX06 owns scripts/build-census-v1-oh_marijuana_expungement-set.mjs, which is a 3-line re-export; the OH family is built by scripts/build-census-v1-nj_arrest_no_conviction-set.mjs.
FIX06 holds il-exp-pardon-set but its owned-scripts list does not name any Illinois builder.
FIX07 and FIX08 own Illinois shims whose host, scripts/build-census-v1-il-exp-pardon-set.mjs, is unowned.
ownedPathsDidNotCoverTheAssignedRepairs.howThisDispatchHandledIt: Where a repair could not be performed inside the named paths, the shared host was edited with the per-family opt-in pattern the hosts themselves already document, and the containment was then MEASURED rather than asserted: every sibling family on a touched host was rebuilt and its bytes compared. rcap-oh-custom-pleading-clean-tracks produced zero changed files; ak-tf800-set produced byte-identical fixtures after the shared-finalizer change. No live claim was held by any other lane on any host touched.

environment.consequence: Seven of the thirteen families -- both Alabama families and all five Illinois families -- bind at least one source that is indexed only under custody nationwide_recovery_pool_2026_09_02, which this container does not hold. Each of those builds fails its source-custody assertion before writing a byte. The gitignored private/ tree was symlinked from the shared checkout as instructed; it carries the Master Library and nothing else.
